key_concepts: Biological organization is arranged from smallest to largest levels.
Subatomic particles, atoms, molecules, and macromolecules are levels below the cell.
Cells are the basic units of life.
Tissues, organs, and organ systems are levels between cells and organisms.
A population is a group of organisms of the same species in an area.
A community includes different species interacting in an area.
An ecosystem includes living communities and their nonliving environment.
Biomes and the biosphere are the largest levels of biological organization.
Macroscopic levels of biological organization can be observed directly in nature.
Organisms interact with each other and with their environment.
Understanding biological organization helps in conserving ecosystems.
